area: AREA 5: one-person-twice TEXT gates (G-GHOST ghost body-parts, G-TWICE double positions) — plan-level, before any grid, panel or take exists
summary: The root problem: H3 draws every person the text asserts, so a possessive body part belonging to a cast member who is not in the shot's faces ("over the brother's shoulder", "the curate's shoulder") is drawn as a second whole man, and one faces member given two different world anchors inside one drawn surface ("leading the curate into the scullery" + "the curate follows at the kitchen door") is drawn twice — and the writer re-adds both clause kinds on every improve round, so Claude kept deleting them by hand. The mechanism: two new hard battery gates in studio/plan_gates.py (G-GHOST: a BODY_PART possessive whose owner resolves, via a refs.json-derived unique-token table, to a cast member absent from faces; G-TWICE: ≥2 distinct non-screen-space locative anchors for one faces member within one drawn surface, where a surface is frame+at_rest, or end alone, or one cut's pair — at_rest vs end is never compared because motion legitimately moves people), wired into plan_check.py so plan_repair's existing fault_rows/cure_for loop picks them up. Cures: a mechanical ghost_limbs clause-surgeon in studio/plan_cures.py (the exact surgery Claude did: "over the X's shoulder"→"from behind", else drop the whole ;/.-delimited clause, under a 30%-of-field word-count guard) and an llm one_position cure in a new studio/plan_llm_cures.py (workhorse tier through llm.structured, guard_spend armed by a spend_context that plan_repair.main now opens itself, code-side probe re-running both detectors on the rewrite before accepting). The re-add loop dies at plan_ladder.Desk.write: every draft any rung writes is scrubbed by the free mechanical cure before episode_home.write_plan, so the battery never re-judges a draft still carrying a ghost clause, and a matching PICTURE_RULES line teaches the writer the rule up front.

gates.where: studio/plan_gates.py new ghost_limb_faults(episode, names); printed+counted in scripts/episode/plan_check.py main() immediately after the refs load at line 239 (refs = episode_home.read_json(book/'refs'/'refs.json')['refs']), before the MARKS block at line 241 — 'G-GHOST      :' heading, faults 4-space-indented so plan_repair.fault_rows collects them
gates.rule: Over FIELDS=('frame','at_rest','end','motion','camera') of every Shot and every SubShot in shot.cuts, match BODY_PART=re.compile(r"\b([a-z][\w-]*)'s\s+(shoulders?|hands?|arms?|back|head)\b", re.I) (replace ’ with ' first). Resolve group(1).lower() through names (see names_from_refs below); unresolved tokens (boat's, frame's) are ignored. Resolved owner in the surrounding Shot's faces (for a cut: shot.faces + cut.faces) -> clean (a face's own shoulder is legal at plan level; the take-prompt side is already handled by 033597a's own-possessive tagging). Owner a cast member NOT in faces -> fault('G-GHOST', f'shot {s.index}', f"{field} stages {token}'s {part} and {entity} is not in faces {s.faces}", entity, 'a face, or absent'). names_from_refs(rows) is a new pure plan_gates function: for each refs.json row take tokens = id parts >2 chars (plan_gates.cast_tokens logic, line 369) + lower-cased display words >3 chars that are not articles; keep only tokens exactly one entity claims (both Elphinstones sharing 'elphinstone' drop the token — documented miss, their full display phrase is NOT matched by this gate). Calibration lock: ghost_limb_faults must return [] on tests/fixtures/episodes/ep05_plan.json, ep07, ep08 and on a new fixture cut from the hand-fixed ep17 shot 11 / ep18 shots 15,19,20,21 (the fixed texts above are clean: 'his thick palm', 'the curate's shoulder' absent).

gates.where: studio/plan_gates.py new double_position_faults(episode, names); wired in plan_check.py main() in the same block as G-GHOST ('G-TWICE      :' heading)
gates.rule: Surfaces per shot: [('frame+at_rest', s.frame+'. '+s.at_rest), ('end', s.end)] plus ('cut@{at_s} frame+at_rest', c.frame+'. '+c.at_rest) per cut. NEVER compare at_rest against end: motion legitimately moves a person between those two drawn pictures. Within one surface: split clauses on r'[;.]'; a clause belongs to a faces member when a unique token of that member (names table restricted to this shot's faces) occurs in it; its anchor is the first LOCATIVE=re.compile(r'\b(?:at|by|beside|against|behind|before|under|beneath|near|inside|into|in|on|upon)\s+(?:the|a|an|his|her|its)?\s*([a-z][\w-]{3,})', re.I) hit's noun, lower-cased, rstrip('s'). Skip anchors that are screen-space placements SCREEN_ANCHORS={'frame','edge','centre','center','left','right','third','half','foreground','background','corner','height'}, another cast token, a pronoun, or a BODY_PART word ('one step behind his LEFT side' anchors nothing). Two anchors are THE SAME when either's first 4 letters prefix the other (door/doorway never conflict). >=2 distinct anchors for one person in one surface -> fault('G-TWICE', f'shot {s.index}', f"{surface} places {entity} at both {a1!r} and {a2!r}; one person holds one position per picture", 2, 1). The fault text carries the surface name so the cure knows which fields to rewrite.

cures.fault: G-GHOST (ghost body-part clause; also the writer re-adding it after every improve/fresh_brief/model_tier round)
cures.how: studio/plan_cures.py new ghost_limbs(doc, names, rewrite=None), 3 helpers each 10-20 lines. Pass 1: OVER_GHOST=re.compile(r"\bover\s+(?:the\s+)?([a-z][\w-]*)'s\s+shoulders?\b", re.I) — when the owner resolves to a non-faces cast member, substitute the phrase with 'from behind' (keeps the camera position, deletes the body; G-MOVES over_shoulder id at plan_gates.py:719 then no longer claims the shot — correct, the shot was never a legal over-shoulder). Pass 2: for every remaining BODY_PART ghost hit, drop the whole enclosing clause: split the field on r'(?<=[;.])\s*' keeping delimiters, drop each segment containing a hit, rejoin, collapse r';\s*;' and leading separators (the exact '; the X's shoulder ...' surgery Claude ran on ep18 15/19/21). GUARD: GHOST_STRIP_SHARE=0.30 — if the dropped words exceed 30% of the field's words, or frame/at_rest would fall under 10 words, restore the original field and hand (shot_index, field) to the injected rewrite callable when one is given, else leave it (the battery re-flags it next round and the row ages into the llm cure via plan_repair). Idempotent: a cured field has no ghost hit left. Dispatcher: prepend (re.compile(r'G-GHOST'), 'ghost_limbs') to CURES at studio/plan_cures.py:326. plan_repair.apply (scripts/episode/plan_repair.py:68-102) gains names = pc.names_from_refs(episode_home.read_json(book/'refs'/'refs.json')['refs']) (guarded by exists(); {} disables both cures and both gates stay creative) and the branch elif name=='ghost_limbs': doc = pc.ghost_limbs(doc, names, rewrite=plan_llm_cures.rewriter(doc, names)). HOOK (c), the re-add killer: studio/plan_ladder.py Desk.write lines 186-187 — after self.pending=None, replace episode_home.write_plan(self.plan, episode.model_dump()) with doc=episode.model_dump(); doc=plan_cures.ghost_limbs(doc, self._names()); episode_home.write_plan(self.plan, doc). New Desk._names(): cached; reads self.ctx.book_dir/'refs'/'refs.json' inside try/except returning {} (tests with SimpleNamespace ctx keep passing; ghost_limbs with names={} is a no-op). This runs on EVERY rung's draft — improve, fresh_brief, model_tier, resume — so a re-added clause is dead before battery() (step_02_plan.py:89) re-judges, at $0, and write_plan's contract validation still guards the scrub (deletion cannot introduce negations or slow words; the guard keeps required fields non-empty). Prevention, same commit: append to plan_brief.PICTURE_RULES (studio/plan_brief.py:44-76): "A body part belongs only to a face in the SAME shot (G-GHOST): never 'over the brother's shoulder' or 'the curate's shoulder enters the frame' unless that person is in faces -- an unstaged man's shoulder is drawn as a second whole man. Each person holds ONE position per drawn picture (G-TWICE): place a man once in frame+at_rest and once in end; two different anchors ('into the scullery' and 'at the kitchen door') double him."

cures.fault: G-TWICE (one faces member, two positions in one drawn surface) and G-GHOST fields the word-count guard refused to strip
cures.est_cost_usd: ~0.001 per shot-call on workhorse (gpt-5.6-luna $0.20/M in, $1.20/M out; ~1.5k tokens in, ~400 out); worst case ~$0.02/episode, guarded by guard_spend against money.episode_ceiling_usd=3.00
cures.how: New module studio/plan_llm_cures.py. pydantic model: class ShotPositions(BaseModel): frame: str; at_rest: str; end: str. one_position(doc, rows, names, caller=None): shot indices via plan_repair.shot_indices-style regex over the rows; per shot, up to 3 asks: result = llm.structured('workhorse', prompt, ShotPositions, _agent=caller) (the _agent seam is the FakeModel test seam, llm.py:269); then a CODE-SIDE PROBE before accepting — build a SimpleNamespace shot clone with the three returned fields and the original faces/cuts and run plan_gates.ghost_limb_faults + double_position_faults on a one-shot probe episode, plus a word budget (each returned field 0.6x-1.4x the original field's words, non-empty frame/at_rest) and episode_spec.negations/slow_word over the three fields; a failing probe re-asks with llm.re_ask(prompt, Exception(probe lines)); after 3 failures the shot keeps its original fields (the battery re-flags, the existing DEFER terminal stands — never a crash, never a hand edit). llm.OverBudget is caught and the shot kept as-is with the row printed as remaining. Dispatcher: prepend (re.compile(r'G-TWICE'), 'one_position') to CURES; plan_repair.apply branch elif name=='one_position': doc = plan_llm_cures.one_position(doc, [r for r in rows if pc.cure_for(r)=='one_position'], names). rewriter(doc, names) returns a callable(shot_index, field) closing over one_position for ghost_limbs' guard fallback. SPEND GUARD ARMING: plan_repair runs as a subprocess (step_02_plan.py:176 ctx.capture_script), so the runner's spend_context does not reach it and guard_spend (llm.py:139) would silently no-op; plan_repair.main (scripts/episode/plan_repair.py:105) therefore wraps its rounds loop (lines 117-134) in llm.spend_context(db.get_connection(), book.name.split('_',1)[0], 'episode', '02', unit=episode_run.unit_of(number)) inside try/except (a missing db/ in a bare checkout degrades to unguarded-but-recorded-nothing only when no conn opens — log a WARNING line in that case, never crash the repair). plan_repair.apply's cure loop runs the cures in ROUNDS=6 battery rounds exactly as today, so a cure that converges slowly is bounded.

NEW fixture: 6 synthetic shots in contract shape — the ep17-shot-11 pattern ('over the brother's shoulder', faces=['captain']), the ep18-15/19/21 trailing-clause pattern ('; the curate's shoulder enters the lower LEFT'), the ep18-shot-20 two-anchor pattern ('into the scullery' / 'at the kitchen door'), and three clean controls including an own-possessive ('the captain's hand') and an at_rest-vs-end move. tests/test_one_man_keeps_one_position.py — plan_gates.double_position_faults: scullery-vs-kitchen-door in frame+at_rest fires one G-TWICE naming both anchors; at_rest 'at the window' with end 'at the door' is clean (motion moved him); 'at the LEFT frame edge' + 'at the kitchen door' is clean (screen-space anchor skipped); 'door' vs 'doorway' is clean (4-letter prefix rule); a cut surface fires independently of its parent.

tests/test_the_position_rewrite_keeps_one_position.py — plan_llm_cures.one_position with a canned-output fake caller (no paid API): a good ShotPositions lands in the doc's shot; a canned output still carrying two anchors is probed, re-asked (fake returns good on ask 2, and the re-ask prompt contains the probe's fault line), and a fake that fails all 3 asks leaves the original fields; a fake raising llm.OverBudget leaves the doc unchanged and does not raise.

tests/test_the_dispatcher_routes_ghost_and_twice.py — plan_cures.cure_for('    G-GHOST shot 11: ...')=='ghost_limbs', cure_for('    G-TWICE shot 20: ...')=='one_position', and the existing creative row still maps to None.

tests/test_a_rewritten_plan_is_scrubbed_before_it_is_rejudged.py — plan_ladder.Desk.write with a fake agent whose draft re-adds a ghost clause, ctx pointing at a tmp_path book carrying a 2-row refs.json: the plan.json written to disk carries no ghost clause (the re-add died before any battery), and the same Desk with a ctx lacking refs.json writes the draft verbatim.

tests/test_the_gates_pass_the_judged_plans.py — ghost_limb_faults and double_position_faults return [] over tests/fixtures/episodes/ep05_plan.json, ep07_plan.json and ep08_plan.json under a names table built from their own cast ids (the calibration lock: a gate that refuses the owner-judged episodes is one somebody switches off). All seven files: pure code + fixtures + fakes; zero paid calls.
risks: G-TWICE anchor heuristics can false-positive on prose that legally names one person near two object anchors in one clause-pair; the calibration-lock test over ep05/07/08 fixtures is the tripwire, and the cure is an llm rewrite whose probe accepts any single-position result, so a false fire costs ~$0.001 and a harmless rewrite, never a deferral by itself.

Shared name tokens (both Elphinstone sisters) drop out of the unique-token table, so a ghost possessive of a shared-surname character is invisible to G-GHOST at plan level; the take-side bind (episode_ref_official.called, full-display rule) still catches the staged half, but the unstaged-ghost half is a documented miss — full-display-phrase matching is the follow-up if an episode pays for it.

The llm cure runs inside plan_repair's subprocess, so the spend guard depends on plan_repair.main opening its own spend_context; if db/ is absent the calls go unguarded (logged WARNING) — acceptable only because the cure's ceiling-per-episode is ~$0.02, but the implementer must not silently drop that context block.

A writer that keeps re-authoring G-TWICE (not mechanically scrubbable in Desk.write) is bounded by the ladder (improve x2, fresh_brief, model_tier) plus plan_repair's ROUNDS=6 and ends in today's DEFER terminal — self-curing fails closed to a parked unit, never to a doubled render, but a pathological chapter could still park.

Signed/grandfathered/rendered plans never meet the new walls (step_02 done()/report() short-circuits), yet any mid-flight plan whose signature lapses on the next write_plan will: expect a one-time wave of G-GHOST/G-TWICE rows on in-progress episodes, all curable by the two cures.

The scrub in Desk.write runs before write_plan's contract validation; clause deletion cannot add negation/slow words and the guard keeps required fields non-empty, but the implementer must keep the scrub INSIDE the try-less path so a scrub bug surfaces as write_plan's loud SystemExit, not a silent skip.
